title: Introduce Budgeted Swing batcher and quantization gradualizer with pragmatic defaults
author: Amira Patel
description:
Motivation: Production workloads with tight monthly budgets need a graceful way to trade cost vs latency without global policy churn. This PR adds a new batcher variant (Budgeted Swing) that targets a budget window rather than hard limits, plus a quantization gradualizer that applies conservative quant tiers on a ramp schedule. Goals: 1) provide safe defaults that improve unit economics for bursty, mid-tail workloads; 2) allow tenants to opt-in via a single flag; 3) ensure graceful fallbacks (no hard degradation) and telemetry to verify regressions.

What this contains (high-level):
- runtime/batcher/swing_batcher.go: new batcher implementing budget-windowed batching and swing lanes (fast/slow lanes that dynamically move requests based on short-term budget pressure).
- runtime/quant/gradualizer.go: conservative quant tier ramper that steps down precision on an exponential schedule when budget pressure persists for N consecutive windows.
- api/defaults/presets.yaml: pragmatic tenant default that enables the mode off-by-default; includes tuning knobs (window_ms, swing_threshold_pct, quant_step_ms).
- console/ui: read-only dashboard fragment for 'Budget Pressure' and 'Quant Ramp Progress' (observability hooks).
- e2e/test_prefill_budgeted_swing.py: integration smoke tests exercising canary L7 policy and fallback.

Design notes: Budgeted Swing uses a sliding window meter (configurable, default 60s) and computes a short-term spend delta relative to the assigned budget runway. When spend > threshold, new requests are preferentially steered to the slow lane which groups and prefetches prefixes (prefill-friendly) while the fast lane preserves SLOs for critical routes. The quantization gradualizer starts at a safe high-precision profile (fp16/int8-mixed) and after K windows steps toward more aggressive quant tiers. All steps are reversible and recorded in the telemetry trace.

Checklist: 
- [x] Implementation of swing batcher and gradualizer
- [x] Unit tests for lane assignment and reversal logic
- [x] Integration tests for fallback paths and no-data regressions
- [x] Console widgets + telemetry metrics (budget.pressure, quant.ramp_level)
- [x] Docs stub and changelog entry

files changed (high level): runtime/batcher/swing_batcher.go, runtime/quant/gradualizer.go, runtime/metrics/metrics_defs.go, api/defaults/presets.yaml, console/partials/budget_pressure.html, tests/e2e/test_prefill_budgeted_swing.py, docs/whats-new/budgeted-swing.md, examples/tenant-optins/enable-budgeted-swing.yaml

Migration and opt-in: The feature is behind a tenant opt-in flag (defaults.yaml sets opt_in=false). No tenant will be affected unless they explicitly enable the preset. For Dedicated customers, the tenant-override CLI can flip the flag cluster-wide.

Risks and mitigations:
- Quality regression risk when quant steps are applied: mitigated by conservative default ramp (3 windows) and offline eval recommends sets based on heldout prompts. We also expose an immediate rollback endpoint.
- Latency SLO regressions for tail-sensitive routes: fast lane preserves low-latency routing and is only affected when budget pressure is severe. We also added a per-route override to keep specific routes immune.

Related: ENG-4678 tracks the long-running roadmap for budget-aware routing; SUP-1229 was a customer request for budget-graceful degradation.

Next steps after merge: run 2-week shadow rollout across 3 sandbox tenants, collect telemetry, and follow up with a policy shortpaper and recommended presets for common SaaS workloads.
